nodes.label: Platform Adapter Plugin Architecture
nodes.rationale: The platform layer is a registry of adapters implementing PlatformAdapter (app/platforms/base.py) so adding Instagram Reels or TikTok is a new folder under app/platforms/, not a rewrite. Adapters return shared dataclasses rather than raw API responses, which keeps the queue, statistics, dashboard, accounts page and permission model platform-neutral; tests/test_platforms.py enforces the contract.

nodes.label: The Money Rule (Monetisable Running Mix)
nodes.rationale: The PRD requires the majority of published videos to be able to make money. content_service implements this as a running mix over the last 20 automatic uploads rather than a fixed rotation, because a fixed rotation cannot self-correct. If the preferred licence class is empty it falls back to the other rather than waste a publishing slot - the ratio self-corrects on the next pick. Owned or commercially licensed counts as monetisable; royalty-free is publishable view-bait; unverified is never published.

nodes.label: Publish Gate (Video.blocking_reasons)
nodes.rationale: The gate is deliberately evaluated twice - once when the job is queued and again immediately before the transfer - so approval withdrawn while a job sat in the queue still stops the upload.

nodes.label: Shorts Formatting Pipeline
nodes.rationale: YouTube decides whether an upload is a Short by inspecting the file (vertical, at most three minutes), not by an API flag, so video_processing.py must do the real work before upload: probe() honours rotation metadata so a phone video is measured as it will actually play, shorts_problems() reports disqualifiers in plain language, and convert_to_shorts() re-encodes to 1080x1920 H.264+AAC with +faststart in blur, crop or pad style.

nodes.label: View-Velocity Trend Ranking
nodes.rationale: youtube/trends.py ranks the mostPopular chart by views divided by hours since publication rather than raw views, because a three-day-old video with 400k views says more about what is rising now than a two-month-old one with 2M. Scores are normalised to 0-100 so separate runs are comparable. Only the topic and its keywords are kept, never the file, to avoid reused content.

nodes.label: Append-Only Statistics Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Each collection appends a StatSnapshot instead of overwriting a counter. That costs a little disk and buys the growth curve, 'views in the last 7 days', and an audit of when a number changed. Data API metrics are always available; Analytics API metrics are best-effort because a brand new channel has no analytics rows and that must not stop view counts being recorded. The maintenance job prunes anything over 400 days old.

nodes.label: Bitmask Permission and Role Model
nodes.rationale: Twelve permission bits stored as one integer. A Role carries a bitmask (Administrator, Editor, Analyst seeded); a User points at one role and may hold extra permissions on top so a one-off grant does not need a whole new role. is_admin short-circuits every check so 'admin should have every access' holds even for permissions added in a future version. Guard rails prevent removing your own admin flag, disabling your own account, or demoting the last administrator.

nodes.label: Web/Worker Scheduler Split
nodes.rationale: The web service runs with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=0 and worker.py with 1. With three gunicorn workers each running its own APScheduler instance, the same video would be planned and published three times.

nodes.label: The Request Path
nodes.rationale: browser to nginx (TLS termination, HTTP->HTTPS redirect, static files, upload limits) to gunicorn (3 workers) to create_app(); then before_request force HTTPS and password change, Flask-Login session to current_user, @permission_required bitmask check, thin blueprint view, after_request security headers.

nodes.label: Thin Views over a Service Layer
nodes.rationale: Views are deliberately thin - they parse the request, call one service and render. Anything that decides something lives in app/services/, which is what lets the scheduler reuse the exact same code paths as the website ('one queue, one code path, two triggers').

nodes.label: Background Automation Jobs
nodes.rationale: Four recurring APScheduler jobs: upload_queue (5 min), collect_statistics (3 h), research_trends (6 h), maintenance (daily 03:30 UTC). Every job is also runnable on demand from the dashboard 'Run now' or from the command line via flask run-job, so there is a single code path with two triggers.

nodes.label: Retryable vs Permanent Upload Failure
nodes.rationale: process_due_jobs() classifies failures: retryable errors back off 5/15/45/135 minutes and try again (this is what makes a quota exhaustion self-healing), while permanent errors mark the job failed and flag the account so a human looks at it.

nodes.label: Content Rights Policy
nodes.rationale: Refusing unverified material is not caution for its own sake - it is what makes the 'make money' goal achievable. YouTube's Partner Programme rejects channels built on reused content, so re-uploading someone else's video is the fastest route to denied monetisation, copyright strikes and channel termination. Hence trend research collects topics to film, not files to repost; every video records provenance and licence; a named reviewer confirms rights and that confirmation is written to the audit log; royalty-free attribution lines are appended to the description automatically as CC-BY and most stock licences require.

nodes.label: Fernet OAuth Token Encryption at Rest
nodes.rationale: OAuth tokens are encrypted with Fernet (app/security/crypto.py) before they touch the database and are never rendered in a page. ENCRYPTION_KEY is the only way to read them, so it must be backed up with the database; losing it means reconnecting every channel by hand.

nodes.label: Security Hardening Notes
nodes.rationale: Werkzeug password hashing with an eight-failure 15-minute lockout and identical messages for wrong password and unknown user (no account enumeration); CSRF on every form with state-changing actions POST-only including sign-out; HTTP-only SameSite=Lax sessions, Secure when TLS is on; CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy. The CSP can be strict because the interface ships its own CSS and JS with no CDN, which also means it works on a server with no outbound internet access. ?next= is validated as a same-site path so the login form cannot bounce somebody off-site. Production refuses to start with a missing or placeholder SECRET_KEY or ENCRYPTION_KEY.

nodes.label: .env Machine Configuration
nodes.rationale: Two kinds of configuration are kept deliberately apart. .env belongs to the machine - secrets, paths, ports - and needs a restart to take effect.

nodes.label: Settings Page Operational Configuration
nodes.rationale: The Settings page belongs to the operation, not the machine: editable in the browser and applied on the next background cycle with no restart - automatic publishing, uploads per day, publishing slots, minimum spacing, monetisable ratio, rights confirmation requirement, #Shorts and attribution handling, default privacy and category, trend region, conversion style.

nodes.label: Flask CLI Command Reference
nodes.rationale: init-db, create-admin, reset-password, list-users, run-job, check, db upgrade. Run from the install directory with FLASK_APP=wsgi.py set.
